title: Auto-rollback on SLO breach — Launch Checklist (Release Eng)
content:
Doc owner: Connor O’Brien (Release Eng)
Last reviewed in launch sync: 2025-03-18

Purpose
- Checklist for enabling Auto-rollback on SLO breach integration.
- Covers: feature flags, staged cohorts, comms, rollback plan for the FEATURE (not the model rollout), and sign-offs.

Release train assumptions
- Release window: Tue/Thu 10:00–14:00 PT preferred.
- On-call coverage: Platform Control Plane (primary), SRE (secondary).
- No broad enablement on Fri or within 24h of major infra maintenance.

Key links (fill in as finalized)
- Confluence PRD: (TBD link)
- Confluence design spec: (TBD link)
- Runbook: (TBD link) “Runbook: Auto-rollback on SLO breach”
- Dashboards: (TBD link) “Rollout SLO dashboards and alerting”
- Incident bot channel: #incidents + #eng-oncall
- Console rollout page: (TBD internal URL)

Scope reminder (what we are launching)
- Rollout controller evaluates latency + error SLO monitors per route/model/region/tier and can automatically revert traffic split to last stable.
- Emits audit log events + notifications.
- Console shows policy, health verdict, and rollback history.

Non-goals reminder
- Not quality regressions (handled by eval/quality gates).
- Not auto-rollforward.

========================
A) Pre-launch readiness checks (must be COMPLETE)
========================

A1. Code merged + deployed
[ ] rollout-controller SLO monitor client merged + deployed to staging
[ ] policy schema + validation merged + deployed to staging
[ ] SLO evaluator merged + deployed to staging
[ ] rollback executor merged + deployed to staging
[ ] “unknown verdict” / stale monitor guardrail merged + deployed to staging (explicitly verify)
[ ] audit log event emission merged + deployed to staging
[ ] console backend endpoints merged + deployed to staging
[ ] incident-bot notification formatting merged + deployed to staging

A2. Monitor identity + telemetry prerequisites
[ ] Confirm canonical monitor identity contract is finalized and documented
[ ] Confirm required metric labels are present in prod (route, model, region, tier, customer_id where applicable)
[ ] Confirm monitor naming/labels migration is complete for launch cohort (not necessarily global)
[ ] Validate monitor query templates match SRE SLO definitions (latency + error) for at least:
    - Hosted API
    - Dedicated tier
    - 2 regions (us-east + eu-west or equivalent)

A3. Operational guardrails
[ ] Minimum traffic thresholds set and tested (avoid low-volume false positives)
[ ] Warm-up grace period for new rollout step verified (avoid immediate rollback before caches warm)
[ ] Cooldown window verified (prevents rollback flapping)
[ ] Per-tenant and global rate limiting verified (prevents cascading rollbacks)
[ ] Behavior under monitoring outage verified:
    - Stale/unavailable monitor -> verdict becomes UNKNOWN
    - Confirm executor does NOT rollback on UNKNOWN
    - Confirm we still emit internal metrics and a warning event (non-paging by default)

A4. Audit/compliance readiness
[ ] Audit event types validated with Compliance/Security (Naomi + Marcus)
[ ] Audit events include: who/what initiated (system), policy id, rollout id, old/new traffic split, monitor ids, timestamps
[ ] SIEM export path validated (if required for launch cohort)

A5. Testing readiness
[ ] Synthetic SLO breach test harness passes in CI (no flaky failures for 5 runs)
[ ] Staging game day executed (at least: latency regression, 5xx spike, monitor outage)
[ ] “No-op mode” / dry-run (if available) validated OR explicit agreement to proceed without
[ ] Confirm idempotency keys prevent repeated rollback actions for same breach window

A6. Docs/support readiness
[ ] Runbook is complete and linked from alerts/notifications
[ ] On-call routing + escalation steps in runbook validated by Rafael/Miles
[ ] Customer Support briefing notes prepared (even if feature is internal-only at first)
[ ] Console UX strings reviewed (verdict states, reason text, manual override warnings)

========================
B) Feature flag plan (REQUIRED)
========================

Flags (names are placeholders; update to match implementation)
1) control-plane: rollout_controller.slo_auto_rollback_enabled
- Meaning: When true, controller is allowed to execute rollback actions (not just evaluate).
- Owner: Ethan Park / Benji Okafor

2) control-plane: rollout_controller.slo_auto_rollback_evaluate_only
- Meaning: If true, compute verdict + emit events/metrics, but do not execute rollback.
- Used for initial cohort burn-in.

3) console: console.show_auto_rollback_policy
- Meaning: Show policy + verdict in Console.

4) notifications: incident_bot.auto_rollback_notifications_enabled
- Meaning: Send Slack notifications for auto-rollback events (to the configured channel / on-call).

Flag defaults at start of launch
- Prod:
  - slo_auto_rollback_enabled = false
  - slo_auto_rollback_evaluate_only = true (optional; if shipped, set true for first cohort)
  - console.show_auto_rollback_policy = true for internal-only (or behind staff-only gate)
  - incident_bot.auto_rollback_notifications_enabled = true for internal channels only

Flag ownership / emergency access
- Release Eng can request temporary flag edit permissions during launch window.
- Emergency toggle runbook: “Disable auto-rollback executor” must be executable by on-call in < 2 minutes.

========================
C) Staged rollout cohorts (PROD)
========================

Cohort 0 — Internal only (Day 0)
- Tenants/routes:
  - Redwood internal dogfood tenant
  - 1–2 low-traffic internal routes
- Mode:
  - evaluate_only = true
  - executor enabled = false
- Success criteria (24h):
  - Verdicts emitted continuously
  - Monitor fetch error rate < 1% (excluding brief deploy windows)
  - No unexpected alert spam
  - Console displays verdict history correctly

Cohort 1 — Low-risk external (Day 1–3)
- Tenants/routes:
  - 1–3 low-revenue, opt-in customers (CS-approved)
  - Exclude Dedicated + regulated accounts initially
- Mode:
  - evaluate_only = true for first 24h
  - then enable executor for these tenants only
- Success criteria (48h):
  - Any rollback action is explainable and matches dashboard evidence
  - No rollback loops/flapping
  - Audit events present and complete

Cohort 2 — Dedicated pilot (Day 4–7)
- Tenants:
  - 1 Dedicated prospect/customer with explicit expectation set (PM + CS)
- Mode:
  - executor enabled for cohort only
  - per-region thresholds enabled if requested
- Success criteria (1 week):
  - Meets SRE expectations: pages only when configured; otherwise ticket/noise acceptable

Cohort 3 — Broader enablement (GA gating)
- Expand by:
  - tenant tier (hosted -> dedicated -> private)
  - region
  - route group
- GA pre-req:
  - SRE sign-off after at least 1 week of stable operation in Cohort 2

Notes
- Any cohort expansion requires re-check of “Monitor identity coverage” for the target routes.
- Do NOT enable executor globally in the same change as monitor migration.

========================
D) Launch day runbook (step-by-step)
========================

D1. Pre-flight (30 min before enabling)
[ ] Confirm no active incident / degraded monitoring in target regions
[ ] Confirm rollouts currently in progress for cohort are minimal (avoid enabling mid-critical rollout unless planned)
[ ] Verify dashboards are green and monitoring query latency is within expected bounds
[ ] Post heads-up in #eng-releases + #eng-oncall (template below)

D2. Enablement sequence (recommended)
1) Enable evaluate-only for Cohort 0/1
[ ] Toggle rollout_controller.slo_auto_rollback_evaluate_only = true (cohort-scoped)
[ ] Keep rollout_controller.slo_auto_rollback_enabled = false
[ ] Validate:
    - Verdicts show up in Console
    - Controller metrics: evaluator lag, monitor fetch errors
    - No unexpected audit events (should be evaluation events only, no action)

2) Enable notifications for evaluation events (optional; internal channels only)
[ ] incident_bot.auto_rollback_notifications_enabled = true (internal)
[ ] Validate message formatting includes: rollout link, tenant, route, model, region, verdict, monitor links, runbook

3) Enable executor for Cohort 1
[ ] Toggle rollout_controller.slo_auto_rollback_enabled = true (cohort-scoped)
[ ] Confirm cooldown/min-traffic/baseline comparison settings are correct for this cohort
[ ] Monitor for 2 hours:
    - auto rollback count
    - repeated rollback attempts (idempotency)
    - routing config changes

D3. Post-enable verification (same day)
[ ] Confirm audit events for any auto-rollback action
[ ] Confirm traffic split changes match expected “revert to prior stable” behavior
[ ] Confirm no unbounded notification loops
[ ] Create a short release note in #eng-releases with what was enabled and cohort details

========================
E) Rollback plan (for the FEATURE)
========================

Trigger conditions to rollback the feature
- False-positive rollbacks affecting > 1 customer OR any high-severity customer impact
- Rollback executor repeatedly toggling splits (“flapping”) despite cooldown
- Monitoring dependency outage causes elevated controller error rates or excessive load
- Audit/event pipeline issues that break compliance requirements (missing/incorrect events)

Immediate mitigation (0–5 minutes)
1) Stop further rollbacks
[ ] Set rollout_controller.slo_auto_rollback_enabled = false (global)
[ ] Keep evaluate_only = true (optional) to preserve signal for debugging

2) Quiet notification noise (if needed)
[ ] incident_bot.auto_rollback_notifications_enabled = false

3) Stabilize ongoing rollouts
[ ] If a specific tenant is impacted: disable flags for that tenant only and manually set traffic split to stable

Secondary mitigation (within 1 hour)
[ ] If evaluator is causing load: reduce evaluation frequency / sampling (if config exists) OR disable evaluate_only
[ ] If monitor identity mismatch: revert cohort expansion; fix monitors/labels before re-enable
[ ] If console is misleading: disable console.show_auto_rollback_policy (staff only) and post internal note

Code rollback (last resort)
- Only if flag disable does not stop side effects.
[ ] Rollback rollout-controller deploy to previous stable release
[ ] Validate routing config is stable and no additional rollbacks occur

Post-rollback actions
[ ] Open incident/ticket with timeline and root cause hypothesis
[ ] Capture impacted tenants/rollouts and audit logs
[ ] Schedule a focused game day rerun if issue indicates systemic risk

========================
F) Comms templates
========================

F1. Internal heads-up (Slack) — #eng-releases
Subject: Enabling auto-rollback (SLO breach) for <COHORT> starting <TIME>
Body:
- Change: Enable SLO evaluation (and optionally rollback execution) in rollout-controller for <cohort tenants/routes>.
- Flags:
  - rollout_controller.slo_auto_rollback_evaluate_only = <true/false>
  - rollout_controller.slo_auto_rollback_enabled = <true/false>
- Success criteria: no false positives, no flapping, audit + notifications validated.
- Runbook: <link>
- Dashboards: <link>
- On-call aware: @<oncall handle>

F2. Internal heads-up (Slack) — #eng-oncall
Subject: Launch watch: auto-rollback on SLO breach (<COHORT>)
Body:
- We’re enabling auto-rollback signals/executor for <cohort>.
- Expected alerts/notifications: <types> (internal channels only).
- If noise/impact: first action is disable rollout_controller.slo_auto_rollback_enabled.
- Runbook: <link>

F3. Customer-facing (email snippet; use only for opt-in pilots)
Subject: Enabling automatic rollback protections for your model rollouts
Body:
- We’re enabling an additional safety mechanism that automatically reverts rollout traffic to the prior stable version if latency/error SLOs breach configured thresholds.
- This is designed to reduce incident duration; it does not change your models or prompts.
- You’ll continue to have visibility via audit logs / console history.
- If you’d like to adjust thresholds or disable the mechanism, contact us and we’ll coordinate.

F4. Post-enable update (Slack) — #eng-releases
Subject: Auto-rollback (SLO breach) enabled for <COHORT> — status
Body:
- Enabled at: <time>
- Observed in first <N> hours: <verdict counts>, <rollback actions>, <monitor errors>
- Next step: <expand cohort / hold / disable>

========================
G) Sign-offs (must be explicit)
========================

Required sign-offs before enabling executor for any external cohort
[ ] Product (Rollouts/Console): Marissa Cole or Paula Mendes
[ ] Eng (Control Plane): Ethan Park
[ ] SRE/On-call readiness: Miles Thornton or Rafael Mendes
[ ] Observability/SLO definitions: Allison Grant (or delegate)
[ ] Compliance/Audit (if external pilot + audit commitments): Naomi Feldman

Optional sign-offs (recommended)
[ ] Console backend readiness: Chloe Martin
[ ] Notifications formatting: Hannah Rivera
[ ] Release Eng (final checklist owner): Connor O’Brien

Sign-off notes / exceptions
- If proceeding with evaluate-only without executor: SRE sign-off still required, compliance optional.
- If enabling for a Dedicated customer with contractual SLOs: compliance + SRE required.

========================
H) Post-launch follow-ups
========================

Within 48 hours
[ ] Review false positives/near-misses (even if no rollback executed)
[ ] Tune thresholds / min-traffic / cooldown for cohort (document changes)
[ ] Verify audit log completeness for at least 1 evaluation window and any actions
[ ] Validate on-call load impact (pages/tickets)

Within 1–2 weeks
[ ] Write short internal retro: what worked, what surprised us, what to change before GA
[ ] Decide GA criteria and update PM-482 / ENG-2321 with go/no-go

Open questions (track in PM-482 / launch sync)
- Do we want evaluate-only notifications by default, or only action notifications?
- What is the default fail-open/fail-closed policy per tier (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)?
- What is the max global rollback rate we’re comfortable with during correlated infra incidents?
